doc.name: GreenlandAI
doc.instructions: GreenlandAI — the command centre for the machine economy: ONE keyless MCP endpoint over the live GreenlandAI / JoulePAI / RAREEAI / ENYAL surface (the world graph — companies, resource deposits, infrastructure, projects and commodities, with the relationships between them — and the map; the RAREEAI marketplace + oracle network; wallets; on-chain verification). ENYAL is the identity authority; this endpoint holds no credential — forward your OWN per call. An ENYAL OAuth access token (`eyl_` followed by a JWT, sent as Bearer) works across ALL products; an API key is product-specific (an ENYAL `eyl_` API key is an ENYAL key, a JoulePAI key does not reach the graph, a GreenlandAI key does not reach wallet/marketplace). Send it as Authorization (Bearer `eyl_...`) or X-API-Key; the backend applies auth, scope, ownership and metering. Reads are metered against the CALLING agent's OWN wallet (not the owner's) — read it FREE with the `joules_balance` tool (a GreenlandAI agent key `gai_`/`gqa_` reads its own balance; a `jlp_`/`eyl_` credential reads by wallet_id). CHARGING (one place for every tool that says "Metered"): PRICES come from the API, never from this text — call `billing_quote` (free) with the path for YOUR exact price; it returns `joules` (base), `rail_fee_joules` and `joules_all_in`, the true debit. The bands (greenlandai-api joule_metering.QUERY_PRICING / PER_HOP_JOULES / TX_FEE_RATE): a list, search, nearby, look_from, map_viewport, entity_history or place_index call is the basic class; one entity's record (company, deposit) is the standard class; relationships is priced PER HOP; look_at is its own still price; look_through is that still price per frame; entity_change is two stills; entity_state is its three parts' prices; site_reconstruction is per tier (look/reconstruct_build.RECONSTRUCTION_PRICE_JOULES). The debit is the base plus a 0.5% rail surcharge rounded up (a 100 J call debits 101 J). Metering RESERVES before the call runs and SETTLES after for what was delivered: an empty result settles to zero; a partial traversal settles for the hops delivered; a look_through settles for the frames delivered; a 4xx, 5xx or server exception RELEASES the reservation (nothing charged). A call the backend has already answered SETTLES even if you disconnect or time out — the work was done. Every tool call through THIS server carries its own fresh idempotency key, so calling a tool again is a NEW charge (a cached free replay needs the same credential + key + request within 15 minutes, which only a direct API caller sending its own key gets). WHAT YOU PAID: every metered JSON response carries a top-level `charged_joules` (the all-in PRICE) and a `metering` block written after the settle — {attempt_id, settlement, settled_joules, check}; `metering.settlement` is whether you PAID: settled · settled_zero (empty, nothing moved) · settle_failed (delivered but unpaid — the wallet is locked and the next metered call 402s naming the attempt and what clears it) · released (nothing moved) · unknown; `settled_joules` is what left your wallet. Check every charge yourself with `billing_attempts` (own wallet: reserved vs settled per attempt). An underfunded read returns a 402 with the deficit and the next tool to call — never a website. A GreenlandAI agent funds its OWN wallet with USDC on Base at its own address (GET /api/v1/agent/me/deposit-address with the agent key; `funding_prepare` gives it, `funding_status` tracks it) or is funded by its OWNER (POST /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/fund with the owner's session). Starting from no account: one email verification done by API (no browser), at least 5 USDC on Base, then unattended — the seven steps are in greenlandai.ai/llms.txt (Cold start). A read past the daily cap your OWNER set for you returns a 402 `owner_cap_reached` (or `owner_allowance_required`) instead: not a shortfall, funding does not lift it, nothing is charged; it clears at 00:00 UTC or when the owner acts. ANNOTATIONS: read-only tools change nothing but your own metered debit; the 8 write tools (market_provide, market_request, market_accept, wallet_transfer, oracle_register, oracle_assess, oracle_deregister, contribute_relations) are marked readOnlyHint false, and those that move money or cast a verdict are destructive. Oracle participation is invite-only at launch (a non-whitelisted register returns a structured invite with the apply route). A verify result is ENYAL's index answer, not itself an on-chain proof. Each tool's description is its short contract; `tool_guide` (free, with the tool's name) returns its full guide: every rule and edge case, every parameter in full and the fields it returns.

tools.name: look_from
tools.description: Map pins near a point (lat/lng + radius_km). `entity_type` alone filters to that type; with `id` it anchors the view at that entity. Each pin carries its `source_tier` provenance. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90 (WGS84). Use with lng, or pose on an entity instead.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project.

id.description: Entity id to anchor the pose on (with entity_type).

radius_km.description: Search radius around the pose, in km. Default 100.

energy.description: Include energy-fleet infrastructure (power plants and grid assets). Default false.

include_country_centroids.description: Also return country-centre placeholder pins (entities known only by country). Default false.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: signals
tools.description: The live signal cards: compiled, provenance-carrying observations (lead_lag, network, signature) with severity and the entities they name. Cards appear only while their type is armed; an answer with no cards costs nothing. Observations, not advice. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

kind.description: One signal family: lead_lag | network | signature. Default all three.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. DE); cards about entities in that country.

tools.name: relationships
tools.description: Labelled relationship edges (owns, operates, supplies …) around ONE entity, with tier and provenance: start from entity_type + entity_id (or a name in `entity`), walk `hops` deep, filter by relation_type. `as_of` answers for a past date. An ambiguous name fails uncharged and lists the candidates. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

entity.description: Start entity by NAME: an exact (case-insensitive) match, else a name that contains it.

hops.description: Traversal depth, 1-10 (agent keys). Default 1. The billing unit: priced per hop.

relation_type.description: Only edges with this relation label, e.g. OPERATES, CONTAINS, MEMBER_OF.

limit.description: Maximum edges to return, up to 100. Default 50.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. Pins the start node with entity_id.

entity_id.description: The start entity's numeric id (with entity_type) — the unambiguous way to name it.

as_of.description: Answer for a past date: YYYY-MM-DD or a UTC datetime.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: nearby
tools.description: Entities near a location: lat + lng, radius_km, an optional entity_type, limit. Each carries `source_tier`. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90 (WGS84). Required.

lng.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180 (WGS84). Required.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. Optional filter; default all four.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Up to 100. Default 20.

include_country_centroids.description: Also return country-centre placeholder pins (entities known only by country). Default false.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: map_viewport
tools.description: Everything inside a bounding box (min_lat, min_lng, max_lat, max_lng): the true count per type for the whole box plus a capped sample of pins. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

min_lat.description: South edge of the bounding box (latitude). Send all four edges together.

min_lng.description: West edge of the bounding box (longitude).

max_lat.description: North edge of the bounding box (latitude).

max_lng.description: East edge of the bounding box (longitude).

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. Default all four.

energy.description: Include energy-fleet infrastructure and projects. Default false.

include_country_centroids.description: Also return country-centre placeholder pins (entities known only by country). Default false.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: look_at
tools.description: A satellite still of a place: the newest Sentinel-2 archive image on or before `as_of`, by lat/lng or entity_type + id. Returns the JPEG plus provenance (`observed_at` is the scene's date). A cloudy or missing scene is `available:false` and costs nothing. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90 (WGS84). Use with lng, or pose on an entity instead.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. With `id`, anchors the still on that entity.

id.description: Entity id to anchor on (with entity_type).

as_of.description: Newest scene on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the newest scene.

max_cloud.description: Maximum cloud cover of a scene, 0-100 percent. Default 20.

tools.name: look_through
tools.description: An ordered stack of dated Sentinel-2 stills of one site from t0 to t1, one per window (max_frames, default 6), each with its own scene date. A window with no clear scene is an explicit empty frame, not charged. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

t0.description: Start of the date range, YYYY-MM-DD, on or after 2015-06-23. Required.

t1.description: End of the date range, YYYY-MM-DD. Default today.

max_frames.description: How many equal windows to cut the range into, 1-12; one still per window. Default 6.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project.

id.description: Entity id to anchor on (with entity_type).

max_cloud.description: Maximum cloud cover of a scene, 0-100 percent. Default 20.

tools.name: entity_history
tools.description: The cheap index of one entity's dates: imagery scene dates (no images), our record's versions since record time began, and a short newest-first `what_changed` list, each item marked world time or our time. Agent keys. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. Required.

tools.name: entity_state
tools.description: One packet for one entity at a date (as_of): the entity as we held it then, the pins held by then, its relationships valid then, and the satellite still for that date. Charged for the parts delivered. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. Required.

as_of.description: The date of the packet, YYYY-MM-DD. Default today.

radius_km.description: Radius for the nearby pins, in km. Default 25.

max_cloud.description: Maximum cloud cover of a scene, 0-100 percent. For the still. Default 20.

tools.name: entity_change
tools.description: The structured change at one site between two dates (t0, t1): per class (water, ice, canopy, pad, stockpile) the area changed, what optical and radar each saw, and a confidence. Read `height_class` first: only repeat_surface supports a volume change. Slow (about 15–60 s): start=true answers at once with a job_id for job_status. Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

t0.description: The earlier date, YYYY-MM-DD, on or after 1984-03-16. Required.

t1.description: The later date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default today.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. With id; or pass lat + lng.

radius_m.description: Footprint radius in metres, 50-2500, overriding the site's held footprint (else a 500 m circle).

max_cloud.description: Maximum cloud cover of a scene, 0-100 percent. Default 40.

same_season.description: For spans of 300+ days, take the t0 frame at t1's day of year. Default true.

start.description: true: answer at once with a job_id (the same reservation, settled when the measurement is done)

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: An entity_change job started with start=true: running, done (with the answer and how its reservation settled) or failed (released). Free. Only the paying wallet can read it.

job_id.description: The job_id an entity_change(start=true) call returned (a UUID).

tools.name: site_reconstruction
tools.description: A dated, georeferenced 3D model of a site (entity_type + id, or lat + lng) with measurements: extent, elevation, slope, pits and heaps with volumes. The tier (lidar_2m or dem_30m) is decided before any charge. Slow (about 15–60 s). Agent keys only. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. With id; or pass lat + lng.

radius_m.description: Half the square's side, in metres, 100-1000. Default 300.

as_of.description: Pick the lidar collection and texture nearest this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

include_model.description: Also return the binary glTF model as model_glb_base64 (a lidar model is about 5 MB as base64).

tools.name: place_index
tools.description: What exists at a place, and when: dated stills, source quotes and measurements within radius_km of lat/lng or of an entity's site, newest first. Each row carries valid_on (world time) and recorded_at (our time). Filter by dates and kinds; paged. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90 (WGS84). With lng; or name an entity.

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. With id, centres on that entity's site.

radius_km.description: Radius in km, up to 50. Default 2.

from_date.description: Only rows valid on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

to_date.description: Only rows valid on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD.

kinds.description: Comma list of row kinds: still, quote, verdict, match, measurement.

entity_types.description: Comma list of entity kinds to include (deposit, infrastructure, company, project).

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: company
tools.description: One company's record by id: the company, the deposits and infrastructure it operates, its relationships with tier and provenance, and `merged` when the id moved. Have only a name? Call `company_search` first. An unknown id is a 404. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

id.description: The GreenlandAI company id: a whole number (known_companies.id, e.g. "4334").

tools.name: company_search
tools.description: Find companies by name, sector or country, to get the id that `company`, `relationships` and the entity tools take. Returns {count, total, companies[{id, name, sector, country, …}]}, one page by limit and offset. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

search.description: Part of the company's name (case-insensitive substring match), e.g. "rio tinto".

country.description: Country as an ISO code or a name; USA, US and United States find the same companies.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Up to 100. Default 50.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: deposits
tools.description: Search resource deposits by commodity, resource_type, country, status, owner_country, max_port_km or name. `commodity` matches through the commodity graph (a group match counts; `commodity_filter` says which). Returns {count, total, deposits[]}, paged. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

resource_type.description: The deposit's primary resource label (exact, case-insensitive).

country.description: Country as an ISO code or a name.

status.description: Deposit status, e.g. operating, development, exploration.

owner_country.description: Country of the deposit's owners (their home states), ISO code or name.

max_port_km.description: Only deposits within this many km of a port.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Up to 100. Default 50.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: deposit
tools.description: One resource deposit by id: its record, `commodities[]` ({name, role, group}) and operators. Pair with `deposits(commodity=…)` to find ids. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

id.description: The deposit's numeric id (from `deposits`, a pin, or a relationship row).

tools.name: market_listings
tools.description: Browse the RAREEAI marketplace: kind="providers" (listings, filterable and sorted) or "oracles". Paged.

resource_type.description: Listings of this resource type only (providers).

oracle_verified.description: Only providers that opted in to oracle verification (true) or did not (false).

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Up to 200. Default 50.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

sort.description: Sort order, e.g. price_asc (default) or price_desc.

tools.name: market_match
tools.description: Read one marketplace match you are a party to: its escrow_terms, fee and timeout fields, dispute window and dispute state. For the settlement legs use `trade_settlement`.

match_id.description: The marketplace match id (UUID). You must be a party to it.

tools.name: market_quote
tools.description: Read one marketplace REQUEST you own, by id: its terms, status and units matched, plus the generic `escrow_terms`. A trade's own fee and deadlines are on the match — read them with `market_match`.

request_id.description: The marketplace REQUEST id (UUID) you posted with `market_request`.

tools.name: joules_balance
tools.description: Your own wallet balance, free. A GreenlandAI agent key (gai_/gqa_) reads its own wallet with no arguments; a JoulePAI or ENYAL credential passes `wallet_id`. The graph meter debits this same wallet.

tools.name: billing_quote
tools.description: The exact price of a metered call for YOU, before you make it — free. `path` = the API path the tool hits (e.g. /api/v1/relationships, with hops). Fund `joules_all_in`, the true debit. The quote says when it is a maximum and when an empty answer is free.

path.description: The API path the call would hit, e.g. "/api/v1/relationships", "/api/v1/look.from", "/api/v1/companies/{id}" …

hops.description: Graph depth for a relationships path (an agent key up to 10).

entity_type.description: Entity kind: deposit | infrastructure | company | project. Alternative to lat/lng for a site.

id.description: Entity id (with entity_type) for a site.

tools.name: receipts_me
tools.description: Receipts for your key: whether THIS key is opted in to a receipt with each paid graph answer, and how its owner turns them on. Free.

tools.name: billing_attempts
tools.description: YOUR OWN charge record, attempt by attempt (your own wallet, from your credential): each attempt's status (pending, completed, settled_zero, failed, refunded …), reserved vs settled joules, and the attempt_id to match a call's `metering.attempt_id`. Paged with limit and offset.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

tools.name: verify_proof
tools.description: Look up one identifier (a chunk, proof, match or transfer id, or a BSV txid) in ENYAL's public verify lookup; its verdict fields come back unchanged. Only `chain_confirmed:true` is a verified anchor; `degraded:true` means inconclusive, not absent. No auth.

identifier.description: The id to look up: a chunk_id, proof_id, match_id or transfer id (UUID), or a BSV transaction id (64 hex).

tools.name: ledger_verify
tools.description: Recent public ledger anchors with their on-chain transaction ids and the exact credit supply at each anchor — public, no auth. Independently checkable.

tools.name: transparency_latest
tools.description: The latest hourly public transparency attestation: a Merkle root over every wallet balance, the verified total supply and the Bridge Ledger root, with the anchoring BSV txid ("pending" until broadcast; `last_anchored` names the newest anchored one). No auth.

tools.name: balance_proof
tools.description: Inclusion proof for YOUR wallet balance in the latest hourly transparency attestation: leaf hash, Merkle path, root, the anchoring BSV txid ("pending" until the batch is broadcast) and how to verify it. No arguments: the wallet is the one your credential owns.

tools.name: bridge_proof
tools.description: Inclusion proofs for YOUR Bridge Ledger rows (contribution and fee events): per-row leaf hash, Merkle path, bridge_root and the anchoring BSV txid ("pending" until the hourly batch is broadcast). No arguments: scoped to your credential.

tools.name: market_request_rematch
tools.description: Match one of YOUR open requests now. Machine speed escrows each match from your wallet at once; human speed waits for the provider's approval. A 409 when the request is no longer open.

tools.name: market_request_rematch_withdraw
tools.description: Withdraw a request's automatic re-matching consent now (DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/request/{id}/rematch). Matches already escrowed stay as they are.

tools.name: market_provide
tools.description: Create or update a marketplace listing (verified account, marketplace:write). Typed body: wallet_id, frontier, resource_type, unit_type, price_joules_per_unit and optional capacity, limits, SLA and oracle opt-in. A first-time registration carries a one-time fee.

wallet_id.description: your wallet UUID: it pays the registration fee and receives payouts

frontier.description: the marketplace frontier the listing is in

unit_type.description: the unit the price is per

price_joules_per_unit.description: your price in joules per unit, a whole number >= 0

min_units.description: the smallest match you accept, in units

max_units_per_match.description: the largest single match, in units

sla.description: your service-level terms, as a JSON object

speed.description: delivery speed class, per the RAREEAI docs

timeout_hours.description: delivery deadline in hours (or use timeout_minutes)

timeout_minutes.description: delivery deadline in minutes (or use timeout_hours)

stake_amount.description: joules you stake on the listing

oracle_verified.description: opt IN to oracle verification of your deliveries (a preference, not a badge)

idempotency_key.description: your own opaque key: the same key and body is one listing change, never two

body.description: The listing; each field is described in its schema.

tools.name: market_request
tools.description: Post a marketplace BUY request (verified account, marketplace:write): wallet_id, frontier, resource_type, unit_type, units_needed, max_price_per_unit and options. Escrow is debited on match. A physical trade must carry `physical_claim` (the site and dates).

kind.description: physical_change: something changed at the site between t0 and t1 · physical_state: the site shows something …

site_entity_type.description: the GreenlandAI entity at the site, if any

t0.description: YYYY-MM-DD; required for physical_change, before t1, on or after 1984-03-16

max_price_per_unit.description: the most a background re-match may pay a unit: 1 .. the request's own max_price_per_unit (default: that …

window_seconds.description: how long the consent lasts, 300-86400 s (default 86400)

wallet_id.description: your wallet UUID: it pays the escrow when the request matches

frontier.description: the marketplace frontier to buy in

unit_type.description: the unit you buy in (the provider's unit_type)

units_needed.description: how many units, a whole number > 0

max_price_per_unit.description: the most you pay per unit, in joules, a whole number > 0

priority.description: matching priority, per the RAREEAI docs

requirements.description: extra requirements for providers, as a JSON object

ttl_seconds.description: seconds until the request expires unmatched

speed.description: the delivery speed class you want, per the RAREEAI docs

privacy_mode.description: the request's privacy mode, per the RAREEAI docs

contract_escrow.description: opt in to the on-chain escrow contract lane (a flat contract fee added to your lock).

physical_claim.description: REQUIRED for resource_type scene_stack, change_report, site_reconstruction or satellite_imagery (refused …

idempotency_key.description: your own opaque key: the same key and body is one request, never two

provider_id.description: the listing to buy from: a provider id from market_listings (kind providers).

rematch.description: MACHINE speed only: allow automatic re-matching if a match on this request ends without delivery, within …

body.description: The buy request; each field is described in its schema.

tools.name: market_accept
tools.description: Accept a delivery on a match (POST /match/{id}/accept) — releases escrow to the provider. You must be the buyer party; the backend enforces it.

match_id.description: The marketplace match id (UUID). You must be its buyer.

idempotency_key.description: Your own opaque key: the same key accepts once, never twice.

tools.name: wallet_transfer
tools.description: A direct wallet-to-wallet transfer (wallet:transfer scope). An agent wallet may send only to a registered destination; limits are live config, not constants. Typed body: from_wallet_id, to_wallet_id or to_handle, amount and options. A transfer fee is charged to the sender. privacy_mode: only 'transparent' (or omit it) — the other modes are temporarily unavailable and refused.

to_wallet_id.description: recipient wallet UUID; send this or to_handle

to_handle.description: recipient handle instead of a wallet id

amount.description: joules to send, a whole number > 0 (the transfer fee is charged to the sender on top)

platform.description: the platform the transfer is made for, recorded on the transfer

note.description: a note recorded with the transfer, up to 500 characters

idempotency_key.description: your own opaque key, 1-128 characters: the same key and body is one transfer, never two.

privacy_mode.description: only 'transparent' is accepted for now (or omit it): 'confidential', 'private' and 'stark_wrapped' are …

registration_id.description: pending service registration id for an agent-class quoted transfer

body.description: The transfer; each field is described in its schema.

tools.name: joules_deficit
tools.description: Can you afford the next call? Give a planned `cost`; returns {needed, have, shortfall, tool_to_call_next}. Free. Agent keys read their own wallet; a JoulePAI or ENYAL credential may pass `wallet_id`.

cost.description: The joules the next call will cost (its joules_all_in from billing_quote).

wallet_id.description: Wallet to read (UUID); omit to use your own. Not used with a GreenlandAI agent key.

tools.name: funding_prepare
tools.description: The in-band funding step for a joule shortfall: your own USDC-on-Base deposit address and the live minimum, read from the running system. It moves no money; track the deposit with `funding_status`.

needed.description: The joules you are short (the shortfall from joules_deficit or a 402). Default 0.

tools.name: funding_status
tools.description: YOUR OWN USDC-on-Base deposit state: credited, or held (below the minimum, above the maximum, or waiting for platform funding) — nothing is lost while held. From your credential, no arguments.

tools.name: trade_settlement
tools.description: YOUR OWN trade's settlement, as buyer or seller: every leg (payout, fees, refunds) with its role, amount, ledger status and on-chain anchor state, plus the escrow contract's legs when there is one. A 404 means you were not a party.

match_id.description: The marketplace match id (UUID). You must have been its buyer or seller.

tools.name: oracle_register
tools.description: Register as a RAREEAI oracle by staking joules (invite-only at launch; a wallet not yet invited is told how to apply). Body: wallet_id, specialisations (1–7 from a fixed list) and stake_amount. The stake is returned when you deregister.

wallet_id.description: your wallet UUID: it holds the stake

specialisations.description: 1 to 7 values from exactly: code, translation, data, general, content, research, infrastructure

stake_amount.description: joules to stake, at least 10,000; refundable on deregister

body.description: The registration; each field is described in its schema.

tools.name: oracle_assignments
tools.description: List YOUR oracle assignments: each delivery to assess, with its match_id, deadline, the fee earned and your verdict if already given. Optional status filter and limit.

tools.name: oracle_assess
tools.description: Post your verdict on a delivery you were assigned: verdict (valid or invalid), quality_score 0-100, notes, an optional execution_trace. A low score opens a dispute. A 409 means the match has moved on — do not retry; read the match.

verdict.description: valid or invalid: was the delivery what was bought

execution_trace.description: how you verified the delivery, as a JSON object

match_id.description: The marketplace match id (UUID). One you are assigned to assess.

body.description: Your verdict; each field is described in its schema.

tools.name: oracle_deregister
tools.description: Deregister as an oracle and get your stake back from escrow (less anything slashed). `wallet_id` is required. Fails while you have pending assessments.

wallet_id.description: Your oracle wallet's UUID (the one that holds the stake).

tools.name: contribute_relations
tools.description: Submit evidenced graph relationships to the contributor door (TEN programme). Each relation needs subject, relation, object, a real source_url and a verbatim quote from it. Nothing is written on submit: admitted claims queue for the nightly judge. Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key.

entities.description: New entities proposed alongside a relation that references them; never accepted on their own.

tools.name: contribute_stats
tools.description: Your OWN contributor standing: submitted, accepted and rejected totals, acceptance rate, pending review and standing (good, warning, suspended, revoked). Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key.

tools.name: contribute_submissions
tools.description: Your OWN per-item submission outcomes: pending_review, accepted or rejected, with the judge's reason verbatim and what was promoted. Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key. Paged.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

tools.name: contribute_receipts
tools.description: Your OWN append-only contribution receipts, each with its canonical claim hash (claim_sha256), so you can check the door holds what you sent. Send your enabled gai_ key as X-API-Key. Paged.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

tools.name: tool_guide
tools.description:
The full guide for one tool, free and not metered: its complete description (edge cases, every rule, examples), every parameter's
    full description and the fields it returns. Each tool's listed description is its short contract; read this when you need the rest.

tool.description: A tool name from tools/list, e.g. relationships.

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: company + relationships + entity_history for one company in ONE call, billed exactly as the three would be, with one charged_joules total. Lean by default; include_raw for everything. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

id.description: The company id (from company_search, a pin or a relationship row).

include_raw.description: Return every part whole. Default false.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.

tools.name: deposit_brief
tools.description: deposit + relationships + entity_history for one deposit in ONE call, billed exactly as the three would be, with one charged_joules total. Lean by default; include_raw for everything. Metered: see CHARGING in the server instructions; quote first with `billing_quote`.

id.description: The deposit id (from deposits, a pin or a relationship row).

include_raw.description: Return every part whole. Default false.

fields.description: Only these keys in each row (plus id). Omit for all.
